text.p: Hungarian autobus-maker Ikarus Rt said on Tuesday that it planned to triple its sales and post profits of four billion forints in 1997, compared with a loss of 3.5 billion forecast for this year.
The Hungarian news agency MTI quoted Ikarus chairman Gabor Szeles as saying that Ikarus planned to sell 2,500 buses next year, compared with the company forecast of 800 for 1996.
Szeles added that Ikarus had already received orders for 1800 buses to be produced in 1997, and the company hoped to win orders for 700 more on tenders, MTI said.
Ikarus expected to increase its sales to 47 billion forints next year from a forecast 13.5 billion for 1996, Szeles said, adding that the company would need to add at least 700 workers in 1997.
Szeles said that the planned increase in sales was likely to enable Ikarus to repay the seven billion forint that it owed to the state, over the next four years, with a one-year grace period.
He added that Ikarus could be privatised only after the reorganisation of the company.
